programme.title: Thank You Sir Kev
programme.desc:
Prince William leads the tributes to Sir Kevin Sinfield for his remarkable fundraising for the MND community after taking on seven incredible challenges over seven years. His Royal Highness, who joined Sinfield on this year’s challenge, has said he is in awe of him and praises his quiet leadership, stating the rugby league legend is ‘a kind caring human being, but he’s still a lunatic’.
In 2020, Sinfield went for a run after his friend and teammate Rob Burrow was diagnosed with motor neurone disease. He aimed to raise £77,777 for Rob and his family, a sum set to recognise Burrow’s number seven shirt. But just a week later, he had raised more than £2 million. It was the first of seven astonishing challenges over the next six years, which included seven ultramarathons in seven days and 101 miles in 24 hours. In total, he has raised more than £13 million.
This touching documentary, made by BBC Breakfast, reflects on what has driven 'Sir Kev'. His parents, Ray and Beryl, talk about his upbringing and introduction to sport.
Former England rugby union captain Lewis Moody and ex-Premier League footballer Marcus Stewart talk about the difference he has made. Moody reveals Sinfield was one of the first people he spoke to when he was diagnosed with MND, while Stewart tells how Kevin rallied a whole community behind him.
Rob Burrow’s wife Lindsey reminds viewers that everyone needs a friend like Kev, while their daughter Macy says Sinfield is a real-life superhero. Rob’s mum, Irene, who first met Sinfield as a teenager, said she had called him ‘Sir Kev’ for many years.
As well as major sporting names, the documentary also features some of those living with MND and reveals how he has changed awareness. More than 5,000 people are living with the disease in the UK at any one time, and many of them and their families have supported Sinfield’s challenges. Some have joined Sir Kevin for a short distance as a way of showing support. Reporter - Sally Nugent Editor - Ben Kay-Coles Producer - Claire Ryan Production Manager - Laura Perrins.

programme.title: Clickbait Clinic with Stacey Dooley
programme.sub-title: Can dog deworming tablets cure cancer ║ S1E6/6
programme.desc:
Stacey looks into an emotive and controversial trend claiming that over-the-counter dog deworming tablets fenbendazole can cure cancer. She meets Mel, a woman from Kent with stage four cancer, who decided to start the DIY treatment and chart her progress on her socials.
Further sleuthing takes Stacey to America to meet Joe Tippens, the originator of the trend, whose claims sparked nationwide panic buying of fenbendazole in South Korea. That leads Stacey to explore why medical trials have never been fully funded, and to ask Dr Alex and Dr Nighat about the potential side-effects and the benefits of sticking to NHS-approved treatments. programme.title: Celebrity Race Across the World
programme.desc:
Four familiar faces paired with a friend or a loved one leave their luxury lifestyles at the starting line for a journey that will take them to the other side of the world and push them to the limits of their endurance. The pairs embark on a life-changing adventure - a 7,500km race from the prehistoric jungles of Borneo to the sun-baked southern tip of Australia.
Competing in this series are acclaimed singer-songwriter and musician Sam Ryder, and his best friend and tour manager, Kaz; veteran sports broadcaster Jeff Stelling and his son Matt; BRIT award-winning singer-songwriter Ella Eyre and childhood friend Nana; and influencer Princess Andre with her brother musician Junior Andre.
Stripped of their smartphones and bank cards, these household names will be tested; emotions will run high, and relationships will be transformed on an adventure that’s as challenging as it is rewarding. They will need to rely on their own resourcefulness and the kindness of strangers to reach the finish line, equipped with only a map and a budget of £26 each a day.
Their race begins in Kuching, a vibrant city in north west Malaysian Borneo and the gateway to the island's vast wilderness. From there, the teams must cross three countries and two continents, weaving through five checkpoints before reaching the finish line in Melbourne, Australia.
The teams must tackle the most formidable race yet - traversing the ancient jungles and indigenous heartlands of Borneo, navigating the Makassar Strait to Sulawesi, an island of cinematic, towering limestone cliffs, before reaching the kaleidoscopic splendour of Queensland's landscapes, from the turquoise blues of the Great Barrier Reef to the arid, expansive orange of the outback. Finally, they will thread through sprawling Sydney before reaching the finish line on the southern tip of Australia.
Musician Sam and tour manager Kaz embrace an unexpected start to the race and dive straight in, relishing the chance to revisit the early days of their friendship when roughing it on tour was the norm. They undertake a jungle adventure, heading inland to connect with the indigenous Tae people.

programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are
programme.desc: Actor and writer Ruth Jones - Nessa from Gavin and Stacey - investigates her Welsh family’s history. On her mum’s side, she discovers that her great-great-great-grandfather was a mariner who rose to the rank of captain in the domestic coastal trade. His son surpassed his father by carrying Welsh coal across the world. On Ruth’s dad’s side, she looks into the career of the grandfather she never met. Henry Richard Jones was a leading light in the Medical Aid Societies of south Wales, which provided a model for the National Health Service in 1948. programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc:
Christina Trevanion goes underground to explore medieval passageways beneath Exeter city centre. In the company of historian Professor Mark Stoyle, she learns how 425 metres of tunnels were built over water pipes to bring clean water to the city’s people in the 1300s.
Above ground, four teams shop for treasures at a huge antiques fair on the outskirts of Exeter. The red teams are firefighters Steve and Andrew, and friends Tricia and Debbie, all skippered by expert Richard Madley. Their opponents in blue are sales assistants Jack and Shaun, and friends Tony and Danny, guided by expert Ben Cooper.
A flock of geese decoys stops Steve and Andrew in their tracks, but the price is sky high, so they walk on by. Meanwhile, Tony and Danny spot a set of bagpipes, but it’s too much of a squeeze on their budget.
With their shopping bags full, the teams travel to nearby Hele in north Devon, where auctioneer Adam Partridge is on the rostrum selling them to the highest bidder.

programme.title: The Northumbria Mysteries
programme.desc:
When an exclusive, high-roller poker night ends with the murder of oil magnate and seemingly devoted family man Jeremy Hare, Rose and Raj find themselves completely out of their depth in the gambling world. The evidence is perplexing. Jeremy’s substantial winnings from the night are still on his body, and he’s been stabbed with an ornate, ceremonial golden knife that was left at the scene. Unfamiliar with the complex strategies and unspoken rules of high-stakes poker, Rose and Raj are left struggling to decipher the various hidden motives of the players around the table.
The game was hosted by Ace Dawso, a slick operator and local villain, with whom Joe and Rose have had a previous run-in. Ace’s invitation-only matches attract an elite, ruthless crowd. There’s Rami Ashraf, an enigmatic Egyptian playboy and seasoned poker pro with secrets to protect; Eleanor Calvert, a sharp stock-market whiz and one of the country’s wealthiest, most calculating women; and Ace himself, who sat out the fatal hand but oversaw the room with a watchful eye. Every player present had something to lose and possibly a reason to want Jeremy silenced.
Baffled by the tight-lipped suspects who can quickly tell that she doesn’t understand the game, Rose soon realises that conventional police work won't crack this case. She has no choice but to recruit Joe, whose history makes him the ultimate insider. Enticed back into the illicit world of gambling, Joe is forced to confront the dangerous addiction that nearly ruined his life. To help Rose read the table and flush out a cold-blooded killer, Joe must walk a risky tightrope, gambling not just with cash, but with his own addictions.

programme.desc:
Young Benjamin’s got an eye for a bargain, Kevin’s hoping the dealers deliver on his Pashley bike, and will the font of all knowledge, Peter, sell off an intriguing family heirloom?
Making a beeline for the bidders today is Benjamin from Leeds. He’s brought a Balinese Ubud painting picked up in a local charity shop. Will his exotic artwork prove a lucky find?
Gloria has come all the way from Forfar to sell her dumb valet. One of the dealers will surely be tempted – if not to sell on, just to keep their many glamorous outfits in ready-to-wear condition.
Who will purchase Peter’s prize-winning miniature church font, designed many years ago by a family member? It’s perfect for the man or woman about town who wants their own ecclesiastical antique but can’t quite fit the full-sized thing in at home. This bijou bargain, on the other hand, would even fit in Ian’s caravan.
Wheeler-dealer Kevin rolls in next, with his iconic Pashley delivery bike. It once belonged to famous listings magazine Time Out, but given his high reserve price, Kevin is in danger of having to cycle it straight back to London.
Last before we shut up shop for another day is Jessica from Newcastle, with her trusty steed – a Dala horse. Originally a children’s toy, in the 1930s these carved and colourfully painted trinkets gained popularity as souvenirs and are now sought-after, mid-century collectibles. programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc:
Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Kev, Alan, Jamie and Simon – take on the Bridge of Lies.
One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies.
They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game.
There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. programme.title: Songs of Praise
programme.desc:
As part of the BBC’s Music Is Black season, renowned choir director Mark De-Lisser visits the new exhibition of the same name at the V&A East Museum and introduces exhilarating new music from the London Community Gospel Choir and special guests.
Mark takes a guided tour with curator Jacqueline Springer to explore how black music and the sounds and songs of the black church have influenced British culture and worship today.
In Manchester, key figures from soul, pop and gospel gather to celebrate the unveiling of a new blue plaque in honour of a remarkable trailblazer, Sister Rosetta Tharpe. Pauline Black, lead singer of The Selecter, tells the story of how Sister Rosetta, known as the 'godmother of rock 'n' roll’, became one of the world’s most influential and pioneering Christian musicians. She explains how she brought church music from America to a wider audience, including in an iconic performance at a Manchester railway station in 1964.
Mark then meets Bazil and Leonn Meade of the world-renowned London Community Gospel Choir, who have been thrilling audiences for over 40 years. Mark explores the choir’s often controversial journey to performing with some of the world’s top artists, learning that faith has always been central to their music.
And there are brand new music recordings especially for the season. In the iconic New Testament Assembly Church in Tooting, the London Community Gospel Choir raise the praise with uplifting worship. And there are powerful solos from West End stars Sharlene Hector and Lawrence Rowe, and renowned soul singer Sarah Brown:

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc:
The roadshow visits Bangor Castle in County Down, Northern Ireland, where finds include an unnervingly lifelike grasshopper vase, chairs that may have been destined for the Titanic and rare Japanese woodblock prints.
Lisa Lloyd is fascinated by a book demonstrating the different needlepoint skills honed by a young girl in the 1800s, including miniature fold-out booties and tie-on pockets, while Susan Rumfitt is dazzled by a characterful gold dachshund brooch.
Will Farmer is delighted to find an art deco opalescent glass vase and dish, while Mark Smith is moved to discover postcards from World War I battlefields, hand painted by a teenage soldier who never returned.
Ceramics expert Serhat Ahmet hears how a ceramic vase in the shape of a giant grasshopper sat for decades in the front window at Grandma’s House in Dublin. Elsewhere, clocks and watches specialist Richard Price is stopped in his tracks by an impressive marble mantle clock that had lived on a bedroom floor.
Furniture specialist Lennox Cato sees a pair of skilfully crafted chairs produced for Belfast shipbuilders Harland and Wolff that may have been destined for the Titanic. Lee Young is impressed by a collection of 25 Japanese woodblock prints of Mount Fuji, bought in 1860 by the present owner’s great-grandfather.
Fiona Bruce learns about the remarkable wartime achievements of one of the members of the family who once lived in the house, Commander Barry Bingham VC, while miscellaneous expert Marc Allum challenges Fiona to correctly identify the function of three mystery objects from his own personal collection. programme.title: Desmond Armstrong: America's World Cup Pioneer
programme.desc:
Desmond Armstrong was the first US-born black player to represent the United States men's national football team at a World Cup. He was part of the squad that did the unthinkable: qualifying for Italia 90 at a time when the US had no professional league and football wasn't taken seriously.
This documentary explores how he got there, the racial tensions of that era and his work as a youth academy coach in Antioch, Nashville, making the sport accessible to immigrant communities against a backdrop of heightened immigration enforcement. programme.title: Thank You Sir Kev
programme.desc:
Prince William leads the tributes to Sir Kevin Sinfield for his remarkable fundraising for the MND community after taking on seven incredible challenges over seven years. His Royal Highness, who joined Sinfield on this year’s challenge, has said he is in awe of him and praises his quiet leadership, stating the rugby league legend is ‘a kind caring human being, but he’s still a lunatic’.
In 2020, Sinfield went for a run after his friend and teammate Rob Burrow was diagnosed with motor neurone disease. He aimed to raise £77,777 for Rob and his family, a sum set to recognise Burrow’s number seven shirt. But just a week later, he had raised more than £2 million. It was the first of seven astonishing challenges over the next six years, which included seven ultramarathons in seven days and 101 miles in 24 hours. In total, he has raised more than £13 million.
This touching documentary, made by BBC Breakfast, reflects on what has driven 'Sir Kev'. His parents, Ray and Beryl, talk about his upbringing and introduction to sport.
Former England rugby union captain Lewis Moody and ex-Premier League footballer Marcus Stewart talk about the difference he has made. Moody reveals Sinfield was one of the first people he spoke to when he was diagnosed with MND, while Stewart tells how Kevin rallied a whole community behind him.
Rob Burrow’s wife Lindsey reminds viewers that everyone needs a friend like Kev, while their daughter Macy says Sinfield is a real-life superhero. Rob’s mum, Irene, who first met Sinfield as a teenager, said she had called him ‘Sir Kev’ for many years.
As well as major sporting names, the documentary also features some of those living with MND and reveals how he has changed awareness. More than 5,000 people are living with the disease in the UK at any one time, and many of them and their families have supported Sinfield’s challenges. Some have joined Sir Kevin for a short distance as a way of showing support. Reporter - Sally Nugent Editor - Ben Kay-Coles Producer - Claire Ryan Production Manager - Laura Perrins.

programme.title: Clickbait Clinic with Stacey Dooley
programme.sub-title: Can dog deworming tablets cure cancer ║ S1E6/6
programme.desc:
Stacey looks into an emotive and controversial trend claiming that over-the-counter dog deworming tablets fenbendazole can cure cancer. She meets Mel, a woman from Kent with stage four cancer, who decided to start the DIY treatment and chart her progress on her socials.
Further sleuthing takes Stacey to America to meet Joe Tippens, the originator of the trend, whose claims sparked nationwide panic buying of fenbendazole in South Korea. That leads Stacey to explore why medical trials have never been fully funded, and to ask Dr Alex and Dr Nighat about the potential side-effects and the benefits of sticking to NHS-approved treatments. programme.title: Celebrity Race Across the World
programme.desc:
Four familiar faces paired with a friend or a loved one leave their luxury lifestyles at the starting line for a journey that will take them to the other side of the world and push them to the limits of their endurance. The pairs embark on a life-changing adventure - a 7,500km race from the prehistoric jungles of Borneo to the sun-baked southern tip of Australia.
Competing in this series are acclaimed singer-songwriter and musician Sam Ryder, and his best friend and tour manager, Kaz; veteran sports broadcaster Jeff Stelling and his son Matt; BRIT award-winning singer-songwriter Ella Eyre and childhood friend Nana; and influencer Princess Andre with her brother musician Junior Andre.
Stripped of their smartphones and bank cards, these household names will be tested; emotions will run high, and relationships will be transformed on an adventure that’s as challenging as it is rewarding. They will need to rely on their own resourcefulness and the kindness of strangers to reach the finish line, equipped with only a map and a budget of £26 each a day.
Their race begins in Kuching, a vibrant city in north west Malaysian Borneo and the gateway to the island's vast wilderness. From there, the teams must cross three countries and two continents, weaving through five checkpoints before reaching the finish line in Melbourne, Australia.
The teams must tackle the most formidable race yet - traversing the ancient jungles and indigenous heartlands of Borneo, navigating the Makassar Strait to Sulawesi, an island of cinematic, towering limestone cliffs, before reaching the kaleidoscopic splendour of Queensland's landscapes, from the turquoise blues of the Great Barrier Reef to the arid, expansive orange of the outback. Finally, they will thread through sprawling Sydney before reaching the finish line on the southern tip of Australia.
Musician Sam and tour manager Kaz embrace an unexpected start to the race and dive straight in, relishing the chance to revisit the early days of their friendship when roughing it on tour was the norm. They undertake a jungle adventure, heading inland to connect with the indigenous Tae people.

programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are
programme.desc: Actor and writer Ruth Jones - Nessa from Gavin and Stacey - investigates her Welsh family’s history. On her mum’s side, she discovers that her great-great-great-grandfather was a mariner who rose to the rank of captain in the domestic coastal trade. His son surpassed his father by carrying Welsh coal across the world. On Ruth’s dad’s side, she looks into the career of the grandfather she never met. Henry Richard Jones was a leading light in the Medical Aid Societies of south Wales, which provided a model for the National Health Service in 1948. programme.title: The Northumbria Mysteries
programme.desc:
When an exclusive, high-roller poker night ends with the murder of oil magnate and seemingly devoted family man Jeremy Hare, Rose and Raj find themselves completely out of their depth in the gambling world. The evidence is perplexing. Jeremy’s substantial winnings from the night are still on his body, and he’s been stabbed with an ornate, ceremonial golden knife that was left at the scene. Unfamiliar with the complex strategies and unspoken rules of high-stakes poker, Rose and Raj are left struggling to decipher the various hidden motives of the players around the table.
The game was hosted by Ace Dawso, a slick operator and local villain, with whom Joe and Rose have had a previous run-in. Ace’s invitation-only matches attract an elite, ruthless crowd. There’s Rami Ashraf, an enigmatic Egyptian playboy and seasoned poker pro with secrets to protect; Eleanor Calvert, a sharp stock-market whiz and one of the country’s wealthiest, most calculating women; and Ace himself, who sat out the fatal hand but oversaw the room with a watchful eye. Every player present had something to lose and possibly a reason to want Jeremy silenced.
Baffled by the tight-lipped suspects who can quickly tell that she doesn’t understand the game, Rose soon realises that conventional police work won't crack this case. She has no choice but to recruit Joe, whose history makes him the ultimate insider. Enticed back into the illicit world of gambling, Joe is forced to confront the dangerous addiction that nearly ruined his life. To help Rose read the table and flush out a cold-blooded killer, Joe must walk a risky tightrope, gambling not just with cash, but with his own addictions.

Making a beeline for the bidders today is Benjamin from Leeds. He’s brought a Balinese Ubud painting picked up in a local charity shop. Will his exotic artwork prove a lucky find?
Gloria has come all the way from Forfar to sell her dumb valet. One of the dealers will surely be tempted – if not to sell on, just to keep their many glamorous outfits in ready-to-wear condition.
Who will purchase Peter’s prize-winning miniature church font, designed many years ago by a family member? It’s perfect for the man or woman about town who wants their own ecclesiastical antique but can’t quite fit the full-sized thing in at home. This bijou bargain, on the other hand, would even fit in Ian’s caravan.
Wheeler-dealer Kevin rolls in next, with his iconic Pashley delivery bike. It once belonged to famous listings magazine Time Out, but given his high reserve price, Kevin is in danger of having to cycle it straight back to London.
Last before we shut up shop for another day is Jessica from Newcastle, with her trusty steed – a Dala horse. Originally a children’s toy, in the 1930s these carved and colourfully painted trinkets gained popularity as souvenirs and are now sought-after, mid-century collectibles. programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc:
Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Kev, Alan, Jamie and Simon – take on the Bridge of Lies.
One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies.
They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game.
There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash. programme.title: Cidsin Granaidh Chalanais
programme.desc:
Gregor MacLeod inherited his grannie’s old cookery book. She had written down over 50 recipes by hand and Gregor has set himself the challenge of cooking his way through them.
Gregor takes on grannie’s recipe for rhubarb and orange jam, using his own home-grown rhubarb. Her trifle recipe also catches Gregor’s eye but he can’t resist putting his own spin on it with amaretti biscuits.
Liver is perhaps not quite as fashionable these days but Gregor attempts grannie’s recipe for liver casserole. He talks to his neighbour, once the village butcher, about how commonly it was eaten and gives his verdict on the finished dish.
Gregor’s uncle hears there is baking going and calls in for a ceilidh to try Gregor’s oatcakes. He remembers his mother’s cooking well so if anyone’s going to know whether Gregor is doing her recipes justice – it’s him.
Fhuair Griogar MacLeòid seann leabhar còcaireachd a sheanmhair mar dhìleab: comhairle na làmh-sgrìobhaidh fhèin air còrr is lethcheud dinnear is greim blasta a dhèanamh. Tha Griogar a’ cur roimhe a’ dol tron a leabhar a’ feuchainn orra.
Sa phrògram seo nì e an t-sili a’ mhol i, le ruadhbhàrr is orainds. Tha e a’ feuchainn air an trifle aice cuideachd - ach cuiridh e a dhreach fhèin air, le briosgaidean amaretti.
‘S dòch’ nach eil grùthan uabhasach fasanta an-diugh, ach tha Griogar ga bhruich mar a bha granaidh a’ moladh. Cluinnidh e bho a nàbaidh, seann bhùidsear a’ bhaile, mu cho tric sa bhathar uairigin ga ithe, is bheir a nàbaidh dha a bheachd air an annlan.
Tha bràthair athar Ghriogar a’ tadhal a dh’fheuchainn aran-corca. Tha deagh chuimhne aigesan air còcaireachd a mhàthar - ma thuigeas duine an d’rinn Griogar am biadh cho math rithe, seo è.
In Gaelic with English subtitles Presenter - Gregor Macleod Director - Ramsay MacMahon.

programme.title: Rurachd (Foraging)
programme.desc:
Màiri Anna NicUalraig agus Liusaidh Cooke – An Còcaire Fiadhain – a’ rùrachd airson tairbheartas nàdair. Tha Liusaidh a’ toirt Màiri Anna dhachaigh gu dùthaich a h-òige, Shropshire, far an do thòisich a beatha an co-bhuinn ri nàdar. Tha iad a’ trusadh bhalgan-buachair nach gabh a lorg an Gàidhealtachd na h-Alba, agus a’ dèanamh picil leotha. Tha iad a’ beachdachadh air àrainneachd gu math eadar-dhealaichte bho an dachaigh an Alba le taic bho athair Liusaidh, a’ tadhal air darach a tha co-dhiù 800 bliadhn’ a dh’aois, agus a’ trusadh eidheann-thalmhainn, lus cùbhraidh a tha càirdeach do phionnd is sèids. Agus tha an còmhnaidh ùine ann airson basgaid ùir.
Mary Ann Kennedy and Lucy Cooke - The Wild Cooke -forage for nature’s bounty. Lucy takes Mary Ann to Shropshire where she grew up and began her life in harmony with nature. They collect fungi that can’t be found in Highland Scotland and pickle them. With some help from Lucy’s dad, they visit an 800-year-old oak tree and forage for ground ivy, a fragrant herb related to mint and sage. And there’s always time for a new basket.
In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Caileag nan Eun
programme.desc:
Tha Caitlin na boireannach òg a th’air a beò-ghlacadh le bhith a’ coimhead air eòin. Nuair a smaoineachas sinn air a’ chur-seachad seo is mathaid nach e òigridh a’ chiad fheadhainn a thig a-steach oirnn - ach tha Caitlin airson seo atharrachadh. Mar sin, tha i a’ falbh air turas mòr mun cuairt Alba, a shireadh daoine òga aig a bheil an aon ùidh rithe fhèin. Anns a’ phrògram seo cluinnear na sgeulachdan pearsanta acasan mu na buannachdan agus mun mhòr-thlachd a tha iad a’ faighinn às a’ chur-seachad iongantach seo.
Caitlin is an avid birdwatcher, but as a young female, she goes against stereotype. Keen to connect with people who share her passion, she sets off on a road trip around Scotland to meet other birders who are defying the typecasts and to uncover some of the personal stories behind the hobby. Together, they share the joys and frustrations of birdwatching as well as the pure exhilaration in spotting a bird that means so much to them.
In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Ath-thogail Notre-Dame/Rebuilding Notre-Dame
programme.desc:
Air an 15mh dhen Ghiblean, 2019, sgrios teine mòr mullach Notre-Dame, a' leagail a saighead, a' briseadh a crùisle agus a' lagachadh a ballachan. Às dèidh bliadhna de dh'obair daingneachaidh, chaidh dà cheud luchd-saidheans dhan chathair-eaglais airson rannsachadh a dhèanamh air an togalach ainmeil seo far a bheil cùisean-iongnaidh is taisbeanaidhean fhathast rin lorg.
Dh'obraich àrc-eòlaichean, eachdraichean agus ailtirean còmhla air a' phròiseact gun shamhail seo: fad mhìosan, rinn iad sgrùdadh air a' chrùisle mheadhan-aoiseach a bh' air tuiteam. Fhad 's a bhathar a' cruinneachadh, a' seòrsachadh 's a' rannsachadh na blocaichean, lorg iad comharran snaidhte sa chloich a bh' air am falach roimhe. Cuimhneachain a dh'fhàg fir bho chionn còrr air ochd ceud bliadhna. An tèid aca air na boghachan is crùislean mheadhan-aoiseach a tha deatamach dha seasmhachd an togalaich ath-thogail?
Nì am film seo taisbeanadh air togail na cathair-eaglais iongantaich seo, a' dèanamh luaidh air comas a h-ailtirean 's a luchd-togail. A' cleachdadh bathar-bog 3D ùr aig a bheil comas gun shamhail, nì luchd-rannsachaidh oidhirp air fuasglaidhean fhaighinn air cùisean-iongnaidh Notre-Dame. An tèid aca air togalach a sheas troimh ochd linn chaochlaideach a chàradh?
On April 15, 2019, a huge fire consumed Notre-Dame’s roof, taking down its arrow, piercing its vaults and weakening the walls. After a year of consolidation work, 200 scientists entered the cathedral, aiming to study this world-renowned monument which holds a series of enigmas and revelations.
Archaeologists, historians and architects worked hand in hand on this unprecedented project: for months, they studied the cathedral's collapsed medieval arch. While collecting, organising and analysing every block, they discovered precious marks inscribed in the stone - until now hidden. The memory of gestures left by men more than 800 years ago. Will they be able to rebuild such medieval arches and vaults, key elements of the structure’s durability?
This film unveils the genesis of this tremendous cathedral, highlighting the mastery of its architects and builders. Thanks to new 3D software, researchers can work to solve Notre-Dame’s enigmas.

programme.title: Meaban and Moo
programme.desc:

Seo tha i ag iarraidh orra trì diofar ghlasraich a lorg fhad ’s a tha iad cuideachd a' dèanamh deiseil airson partaidh Oidhche Shamhna. programme.title: Golf: Mun Cuairt Alba
programme.desc:
Le còrr air 550 raon-goilf tha Alba cliùiteach mar dhachaigh ghoilf. Tha an sreath 6-pàirt seo a’ gabhail turas air feadh na dùthcha gu na cùrsaichean ainmeil agus na seudan àlainn nach eil cho iomraiteach, a’ fosgladh ar sùilean gu goilf. Cluinnidh sinn bho ghoilfearan sean is òg, fireann is boireann, goilfearan dall is goilfearan ciorramach, agus bho chuid a bhios a' cosnadh beòshlaint à goilf.
An t-seachdain-sa, gabhaidh sinn sgrìob-adhair mu chuairt raointean-goilf ann an Lodainn an Ear, agus gheibh sinn a-mach barrachd mu raon-goilf na cloinne ann an Gualainn. Tha am Pro Stuart Martin a’ cluiche an 15mh toll dùbhlanach aig Bearaig a Tuath ris an canar ‘Redan’ - tha iomadh rèidhlean Redan anns an t-saoghal an-diugh, ach seo a’ chiad fhear a-riamh a chaidh a thogail. Agus tha coidse proifeiseanta Keil Beveridge a’ toirt seachad comhairle na seachdaine airson dòigh-cluiche.
Scotland has over 550 golf courses and is regarded worldwide as the home of golf. This series takes us on a journey around the country to explore some of the well-known courses as well as some of its hidden gems, and opens the door to golf. We hear from golfers young and old, male and female, blind golfers and disabled golfers, and from those who make their living working in golf, plus we capture a few tips from the professionals along the way.
We take an aerial journey across East Lothian, from Musselburgh to Dunbar. Pro Stuart Martin shows us how to play the challenging 15th hole at North Berwick called ‘Redan’, which is the original Redan, claimed to be the most copied hole in the world. And professional coach Keil Beveridge demonstrates his weekly top playing tip.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Expert - Keil Beveridge Producer - Patricia Macleod Director - Scott Brown Editor - Jonny Craigmile.

programme.title: Trusadh
programme.desc:
Ged nach eil càil cho nàdarrach ri cadal, tha cuid againn fhathast a’ strì leis. Tha an t-seinneadair is craoladair, Joy Dunlop, a’ dol air turas gus dearbhadh fhaighinn air dè dìreach a dh’fhàg ar cadal ann an droch staids is dè ’s urrainn dhuinn uile dèanamh gus faochadh fhaighinn.
Ann an Srath Chluaidh, coinnichidh Joy ris An Dotair Megan Crawford a tha ag obair mar rannsaiche aig Ionad Cadail Shrath Chluaidh, aon dhe na beagan àiteachan san dùthaich a tha dèanamh rannsachadh sònraichte air cadal. An sin, cluinnidh i mar a tha iad a’ cleachdadh leigheas CBT gus fuasgladh a lorg do dhaoine a tha fulang le tinneasan cadail. Ann an Inbhir Nis, thèid i a choinneachadh ris an saic-eòlaiche, An Dotair Rachel Allan, a bheir dhi tuigs’ a bharrachd air mar a tha cadal a’ toirt buaidh air ar slàinte-inntinn agus thèid i còmhla ri caraid air turas gu Loch Fìne gus faicinn an cuidich uisge fuar is yoga i gus cadal nas fheàrr fhaighinn.
A bharrachd air Joy fhèin, gheibh sinn eòlas air iomadh neach bho air feadh na dùthcha a tha a’ strì le ’n cuid cadal. Bho feadhainn a tha ga fhaighinn duilich a dhol dhan leabaidh gu feadhainn eile a tha ga fhaighinn duilich fuireach nan dùisg, chì sinn mar a tha ar cadal air a dhol air iomrall agus na ’s urrainn dhuinn dèanamh gus norrag fhaighinn gach oidhche.
Although there are not many more natural things than sleep, many of us still struggle to get a peaceful night. Singer and broadcaster Joy Dunlop goes on a journey to discover what has caused our sleep to become so troubled and what we can all do to get some rest.
Joy meets Dr Megan Crawford, who works as a researcher at the Strathclyde Sleep Centre, one of the few places in the country conducting research into sleep. There, she hears how CBT therapy can be used to treat sleep disorders.
In Inverness, Joy meets psychologist Dr Rachel Allan, who gives her an insight into how sleep affects our mental health, and she takes a sleep holiday with a friend to Loch Fyne to see if some cold water immersion and yoga will help her to nod off more soundly.
We come across a host of people from around the country who are struggling with sleep.

Anns a’ phrògram, taisbeanaidhean co-obrachail bho na ‘Sessions’ le Emmylou Harris & Mary Black, Rosanne Cash & Radney Foster agus na gaisgich Èireannach Andy Irvine & Dónal Lunny.

This episode features collaborative performances from Emmylou Harris and Mary Black, Rosanne Cash and Radney Foster, as well as Irish music legends Andy Irvine and Dónal Lunny. Presenter - Julie Fowlis Presenter - Muireann Nic Amhlaoibh Executive Producer - Alasdair MacCuish Director - Iain Macleod Producer - Ewan Duncan Production Manager - Gillian MacLean.

programme.title: Mu Chriochan Hoil (Derick Thomson @ 100)
programme.desc:
Ruaraidh MacThòmais – bàrd, foillsichear agus òraidiche, a thug a’ bhuaidh bu mhotha air cor na Gàidhlig anns an fhicheadamh linn. B’ e an dàrna mac aig Seumas MacThòmais, am maighstir-sgoile agus am bàrd. Chaidh a thogail ann am Pabail anns an Rubha ann an Eilean Leòdhais, àite a bha gu math cudromach dha agus ris am biodh e a’ tilleadh uair is uair na chuid bhàrdachd.
A’ cleachdadh tasglann phrìseil nach deach fhaicinn ron seo, bho àm clàraidh a’ phrògraim Creachadh na Clàrsaich, a chaidh a dhèanamh ann an 1999, tha an craoladair ainmeil, Cathy NicDhòmhnaill, aig a bheil ùidh shònraichte ann an litreachas i fhèin, a’ bruidhinn ri measgachadh de bhàird mu dè bha toirt spionnadh dha MacThòmais agus bidh i ag ionnsachadh mu co ris a bha an duine air cùlaibh a’ bhàrdachd coltach bho fheadhainn a bha gu math eòlach air.
Le bhith a’ comharrachadh ceud bliadhna bho rugadh e, dè a’ bhuaidh a thug Ruaraidh MacThòmais air a’ chànan, dè an dìleab a dh’ fhàg e air a’ chùlaibh agus an d’ fhuair e an aithne air an robh e airidh?
Documentary on Derick Thomson – a poet, publisher, and lecturer who had a huge impact on the Gaelic language in the 20th century. He was the second son of head teacher and poet, James Thomson, and was brought up in Bayble, Point on the Isle of Lewis, a place which was very important to him, and to which he often returned in his poetry.
Using unseen and precious archive, from the programme Plundering the Harp, which was recorded in 1999, broadcaster Cathy MacDonald, who has a special interest in literature, speaks to a variety of poets about what inspired Thomson and she also learns about the man behind the poetry from those who knew him well.
Celebrating 100 years since his birth, what impact did Derick Thomson have on the Gaelic language, what is his legacy and did he get the recognition he truly deserved?
In Gaelic with English subtitles Presenter - Cathy MacDonald Executive Producer - Margaret Mary Murray Executive Producer - Seumas Mactaggart Production Manager - Marion Maclean Producer - Peter Macqueen Director - Alasdair MacLean.

programme.title: Alba fon Talamh/Scotland Underground
programme.desc:
In the Highlands and Islands, Calum explores the caves of Assynt, a Unesco global geopark, before travelling north to Orkney where there is a wealth of archeological underground sites. But it is also an example of the modern use of subterranean sites: oil to service the Scapa Flow naval sites was hidden underground in vast tanks beneath Wee Fea hill. The war theme continues as Calum visits a Cold War underground bunker in Inverness.
Anns a’ Ghàidhealtachd agus na h-Eileanan, bheir Calum cuairt tro uamhan Asainte, geò-pàirc cruinneil UNESCO. À sin, thèid e tuath gu Arcaibh far a bheil beartas de làraich arceòlach fon talamh, ach cuideachd eisimpleir nas ùire den fho-thalamh a chleachdadh. Fo chnoc Wee Fea, tha na tancaichean mòra a bha a’ cumail ola ri làrach a’ Chabhlaich Rìoghail ann an Scapa Flow. A’ cumail ri tèama a’ chogaidh, ann an Inbhirnis tadhlaidh Calum air buncair bho àm a’ Chogaidh Fhuair.
In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Rùm Gu Rùm, Le Erica
programme.desc:
Tha Erica Nic a’ Phearsain air ais a’ toirt cruth-atharrachadh àlainn air seòmaran agus toglaichean le a dealbhachadh sònraichte. Leanaidh sinn i bho thoiseach gu deireadh phròiseactan is sinn a’ faicinn gach pàirt den phròiseas, bho phlana air pàipear gu bhith a’ trusadh stuthan airson crìoch snasail a chur orra.
Interior designer Erica MacPherson is back to transform more rooms, homes and businesses. We follow her process from architectural plans to trawling auction houses and shops for finishing touches.
In Gaelic with English subtitles Presenter - Erica Macpherson Editor - Paul Duke Director - Calum Angus Mackay Producer - Rachel Ellen Mackay.

programme.desc:

Govan Gaelic Choir sings Psalm 91, Kathleen Graham sings the hymn 'Reul Àlainn a' Chuain' and Margaret MacSween tells her personal faith story. Presented by Iain MacKinnon. Presenter - Iain MacKinnon Actor - Rebecca NicIllFhinnein Director - Laura MacLeod.

programme.title: Meaban and Moo
programme.desc:
Bidh Linda a’ tadhal air a caraidean Meaban is Moo sa bhothan aca gus dùbhlain spòrsail a chur romhpa. Seo tha i ag iarraidh orra trì diofar ghlasraich a lorg fhad ’s a tha iad cuideachd a' dèanamh deiseil airson partaidh Oidhche Shamhna. Tha treallaich gu leòr sa bhothan agus feumaidh Meaban is Moo a dhol a rùrach!
Linda visits her friends Meaban and Moo at their hut to set them fun challenges. She tasks them with finding three different vegetables while they get ready for a Halloween party. Their hut is full of junk, so Meaban and Moo just need to have a good rummage! Presenter - Linda MacLeod Production Manager - Laura Deponio Producer - Sarah MacKinnon Director - Helen Scott.

programme.title: Leum Suas air an Sguaib/Room on the Broom
programme.desc:
Tha Lìosaidh NicÌosaig, a' bhana-bhuidseach, 's an cat gu dòigheil a' seòladh air sguab. Tha a' ghaoth mhòr ag èirigh 's tha Lìosaidh a' call a h-ad, an rioban a tha na falt, 's an t-slatag a tha na làimh. Ge-ta, tha triùir charaidean eile a' nochdadh a bheir taic dhi.
The witch and the cat fly through the sky on a broomstick. The wind picks up, the witch drops her hat, her bow and her wand. Fortunately, three more friends come to her aid. Can they rescue the witch from the dragon and will there be room on the broom for all?

programme.desc:

programme.desc:

Tha Gran toilicht' leis an t-Seanair leis gun do sgioblaich e 'n deasg aige, ach e 'g ràdh ri Dan nach b' esan a sgioblaich e. Ach cò an luchd-glanaidh dìomhair, agus ciamar a nochd iad an seo? Because they are a little short of money, and considering cash notes are only little papers with drawings on them, Petit and his friends decide to create their own money and buy anything they want. programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.sub-title: Am Balach a bha ag Ithe Leabhraichean ║ S2E13/80
programme.desc:
Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Martainn Mac an t-Saoir a’ leughadh Am Balach a bha ag Ithe Leabhraichean. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh agus a dhealbhachadh le Oliver Jeffers agus chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Dòmhnall Iain MacLeòid.
A bedtime story for young children. Martin MacIntyre reads Am Balach a bha ag Ithe Leabhraichean, written and illustrated by Oliver Jeffers and translated into Gaelic by Donald John MacLeod. Presenter - Martin MacIntyre.

programme.title: Calum: Cogadh nan Comhlan
programme.desc:
Tha Calum airson a chòmhlann aige a thoirt à Glaschu dhan Òban airson blàr mòr ciùil a tha dol aig a' Mhòd Nàiseanta Rìoghail. Ach, le tòrr fharpaisean agus gainead tìde, chan eil cùisean a' dol mar bu chòir. Leis nach eil e furasda còmhlan a làimhseachadh aig na h-amannan as fheàrr, saoil ciamar a thèid dhaibh leis na dùbhlain mhòra a th' air thoiseach orra...
Calum aims to take his band from Glasgow to Oban for a major musical battle at the Royal National Mòd. However, with numerous competitions and time constraints, things aren't going according to plan. Managing a band is never easy even in the best of times - how will they cope with the significant challenges that lie ahead? Director - Donald Ewen MacKinnon Executive Producer - Bill MacLeod.

programme.title: Belle and Sebastian
programme.desc:

Lynette’s loose lips puts Elaina in danger. How can Belle, Sebastian and the gang save the day? Sebastian - Ellen Macdonald Adele - Mischa Macpherson Cameron - Claire Frances MacNeil Mr Turner - Derek Mackay Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid Producer - May Smart Producer - Mairi Macleod Writer - Alec MacDonald.

programme.title: Seonaidh
Shaun the Sheep
programme.sub-title: Bitzer airson Latha ║ Seonaidh. S4E23/30. Bitzer for the Day ║ Seonaidh. S4E23/30
programme.desc:
Leis an tuathanach agus Bitzer a' falbh a-mach airson latha còmhla ri chèile, tha Seonaidh a' gabhail a' chothruim a bhith os cionn ghnothaichean. Ach tha e a' mothachadh gu math luath nach eil an obair cho furasta 's a bha e an dùil.
When the farmer decides it is time he and Bitzer head out for a bit of man and dog time, Shaun seizes his chance to take charge. He soon discovers that the job is not quite as easy as he first thought.

programme.title: Flix
programme.desc:

Flix wants to prove that he’s an ultimate outdoor cat - just like his dad, Zeno. However his nemesis Burma isn’t going to make things easy for him! Flix - Derek MacIntosh Munchkin - Calum MacKinnon Tabaidh - Claire Frances MacNeil Colza - Mischa Macpherson Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid Producer - May Smart Producer - Mairi Macleod Editor - Phil Reed Writer - Alec Macdonald.

programme.title: Golf: Mun Cuairt Alba
programme.desc:
Le còrr air 550 raon-goilf tha Alba cliùiteach mar dhachaigh ghoilf. Tha an sreath 6-pàirt seo a’ gabhail turas air feadh na dùthcha gu na cùrsaichean ainmeil agus na seudan àlainn nach eil cho iomraiteach, a’ fosgladh ar sùilean gu goilf. Cluinnidh sinn bho ghoilfearan sean is òg, fireann is boireann, goilfearan dall is goilfearan ciorramach, agus bho chuid a bhios a' cosnadh beòshlaint à goilf.
An t-seachdain-sa, gabhaidh sinn sgrìob-adhair mu chuairt raointean-goilf ann an Lodainn an Ear, agus gheibh sinn a-mach barrachd mu raon-goilf na cloinne ann an Gualainn. Tha am Pro Stuart Martin a’ cluiche an 15mh toll dùbhlanach aig Bearaig a Tuath ris an canar ‘Redan’ - tha iomadh rèidhlean Redan anns an t-saoghal an-diugh, ach seo a’ chiad fhear a-riamh a chaidh a thogail. Agus tha coidse proifeiseanta Keil Beveridge a’ toirt seachad comhairle na seachdaine airson dòigh-cluiche.
Scotland has over 550 golf courses and is regarded worldwide as the home of golf. This series takes us on a journey around the country to explore some of the well-known courses as well as some of its hidden gems, and opens the door to golf. We hear from golfers young and old, male and female, blind golfers and disabled golfers, and from those who make their living working in golf, plus we capture a few tips from the professionals along the way.
We take an aerial journey across East Lothian, from Musselburgh to Dunbar. Pro Stuart Martin shows us how to play the challenging 15th hole at North Berwick called ‘Redan’, which is the original Redan, claimed to be the most copied hole in the world. And professional coach Keil Beveridge demonstrates his weekly top playing tip.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Expert - Keil Beveridge Producer - Patricia Macleod Director - Scott Brown Editor - Jonny Craigmile.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc:
Tha Joy Dunlop gar toirt tron tuilleadh cheumannan airson ar misneachadh gus leantainn oirnn a bhith bruidhinn na Gàidhlig. Thairis air an t-sreath seo, bidh i a’ dèiligeadh ri facail is abairtean air measgachadh de chuspairean co-cheangailte ri gach taobh de ar beatha. Leis gun do dh’ionnsaich i fhèin a’ chànan, bheir Joy dhuinn briathrachas a tha sìmplidh agus furasta a thuigsinn. Bidh stiùireadh ann cuideachd a thaobh a bhith a’ cleachdadh abairtean, le eisimpleirean soilleir tro chòmhraidhean goirid.
Coinnichidh sinn ri luchd-labhairt èasgaidh, feadhainn a tha ag ionnsachadh as ùr, cuid a bha fileanta agus a sguir ga cleachdadh agus iadsan a th’ air a bhith ag ionnsachadh fad bhliadhnaichean. Agus bidh Calum MacIlleathain a’ toirt sealladh eile dhuinn air Alba ’s e ann an diofar àitichean air feadh na dùthcha.Lorgar tuilleadh stuthan taic air-loidhne aig www.speakgaelic.scot agus ann an sreath phodcastan air BBC Sounds.
Joy Dunlop guides viewers through the next steps to inspire us to speak Gaelic. Throughout the series, she introduces words and phrases on a variety of everyday topics. A Gaelic learner herself, Joy supports us through pronunciation and vocabulary on topics such as friends, home, work, communication and people’s skills.
We meet diligent speakers who have embraced the language, from new learners to lapsed native speakers and the on-off learners who have improved their language skills over the decades. And, the intrepid Calum Maclean takes us on adventures to hidden treasures around Scotland.
Supporting materials can be found online: www.speakgaelic.scot and in the SpeakGaelic podcasts on BBC Sounds. Presenter - Joy Dunlop Presenter - Calum Maclean Executive Producer - Una McDonald Executive Producer - Calum McConnell Director - Sam Pearce.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc:
Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA.
Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Rathad Ramsay
programme.desc:
Ramsay meets Ian Smith in the village he was brought up, before they head along one of Tiree’s most famous beaches. As they walk along the coast, Ian reflects on his youth and the people that impacted him.
Ian discusses how the Tiree music scene shaped him and brought him success as a box player, and he shares his passion for the island and his pride in setting up the only distillery in Tiree.
San treas sreath de Rathad Ramsay bidh Ramsay MacMahon a’ coinneachadh ri sàr Ghàidheil bho air feadh Alba ‘s iad a’ co-roinn sgeulachdan, cuir luach air nàdar agus a’ cnuasachadh ma beatha.
Coinnichidh Ramsay ri Iain Mac a’ Ghobhainn sa bhaile san d’rugadh e mas dèan iad air tè de na tràighean as iomraitiche ann an Tiriodh. Meòirichidh Iain air làithean òige agus na daoine bu mhotha a thug buaidh air a bheatha.
Leis cho cudromach ‘s a tha ceòl air eilean Thiriodh, innsidh Iain man bhuaidh a bh’aige seo air fhèin agus mar a chuidich e a bhith cho soirbheachail le cluich a’ bhogsa. Bidh an dà chuid a mheas air an eilean agus a mhoit man aon taigh-stàile san eilean fhaighinn stèidhichte follaiseach.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Presenter - Ramsay MacMahon Series Producer - Robyn Low Editor - Mairead Morrison.

programme.title: Sailm nan Daoine
programme.desc:
Tha Rob MacNeacail air turas gus sailm Ghàidhlig a sheinn is a sgaoileadh. ’S e film tarraingeach is togarrach a tha seo mu chumhachd na coimhearsnachd, an teaghlaich is an seasmhachd a tha a dhìth gus cànan a chumail beò.
Thòisich Rob air na sailm a ghabhail ann an Carlops gus comharrachadh ceann-bliadhna bàs athar, am bàrd Aonghas MacNeacail. Ged a tha na seiseanan a’ còrdadh ri muinntir a’ bhaile, tha Rob ga cheasnachadh fhèin a bheil còir aige a bhith a’ teagasg nan salm. Cha do dh’ionnsaich e mar a stiùireas e an t-seinn ach o chionn ghoirid, agus cha deach a thogail san eaglais. Chan eil Rob aig tàmh is e a’ faireachdainn gum feum e falbh air turas gus cluinntinn mar a bhios na Gàidheil a’ seinn nan salm anns na coimhearsnachdan a tha a’ cumail an traidisein beò.
Bheir an turas e bho na h-Eileanan an Iar gu Corcaigh an Iar, a’ leantainn seann shlighean a bheireas ceòl is beachdan ùra gu bith.
Rob MacNeacail embarks on a mission to sing Gaelic psalms. An entertaining and heartwarming film about the power of community, family and the resilience needed to keep a language alive.
Rob started singing the psalms in his home village of Carlops to mark the anniversary of the death of his father, the poet Aonghas MacNeacail. Although the sessions are popular with locals, Rob starts to question his authority to teach the psalms, as he only learned how to precent relatively recently and didn’t grow up in the church.
As spring turns to summer, Rob starts to feel restless and decides to hit the road to reconnect with his Gaelic roots and hear how psalms are sung by Gaels in the communities that nurture the tradition. His journey takes him from the Western Isles to West Cork in Ireland, following well-trodden ancient paths that unravel threads of music and ideas along the way.
In Gaelic with English subtitles Director - Jack Archer Executive Producer - John Archer Editor - James Alcock Executive Producer - Calum McConnell Production Manager - Mhairi Valentine Production Company - Hopscotch Films.

programme.title: Dàna
Scotland's Wild Side
programme.sub-title: Am Monadh Ruadh/Cairngorms ║ Dàna. S3. ALBAE2/4
programme.desc:
The vast landscape of the Cairngorms attracts thousands each year. Coinneach Rankin sets out on a multi-day expedition to learn why its vast mountains are a paradise for climbers, runners and so many others. Along with his partner, Coinneach races up one of the highest mountains in Scotland, undertakes a classic multi-pitch climb, and spends the night in a tiny bothy built in the 1960s.
Tàlaidh cruth-tìre aibheiseach a’ Mhonaidh Ruaidh na mìltean gach bliadhna. Cuiridh Coinneach MacFhraing aghaidh air turas grunn làithean gus tuigsinn carson a tha sreapadairean, luchd-coise agus eile cho measail air na beanntan seo.
An cuideachd deagh charaid, thèid Coinneach na dheann suas tè de na beanntan as àirde an Alba, dìreidh e slighe-sreapa fhada agus cuiridh e seachad na h-oidhche ann am bothan a thogadh ‘sna seasgadan.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Presenter - Coinneach Rankin Executive Producer - Tony Kearney Executive Producer - Jim Webster Executive Producer - Calum McConnell Director - Hamish MacLeod.

programme.title: Ath-thogail Notre-Dame/Rebuilding Notre-Dame
programme.desc:
Air an 15mh dhen Ghiblean, 2019, sgrios teine mòr mullach Notre-Dame, a' leagail a saighead, a' briseadh a crùisle agus a' lagachadh a ballachan. Às dèidh bliadhna de dh'obair daingneachaidh, chaidh dà cheud luchd-saidheans dhan chathair-eaglais airson rannsachadh a dhèanamh air an togalach ainmeil seo far a bheil cùisean-iongnaidh is taisbeanaidhean fhathast rin lorg.
Dh'obraich àrc-eòlaichean, eachdraichean agus ailtirean còmhla air a' phròiseact gun shamhail seo: fad mhìosan, rinn iad sgrùdadh air a' chrùisle mheadhan-aoiseach a bh' air tuiteam. Fhad 's a bhathar a' cruinneachadh, a' seòrsachadh 's a' rannsachadh na blocaichean, lorg iad comharran snaidhte sa chloich a bh' air am falach roimhe. Cuimhneachain a dh'fhàg fir bho chionn còrr air ochd ceud bliadhna. An tèid aca air na boghachan is crùislean mheadhan-aoiseach a tha deatamach dha seasmhachd an togalaich ath-thogail?
Nì am film seo taisbeanadh air togail na cathair-eaglais iongantaich seo, a' dèanamh luaidh air comas a h-ailtirean 's a luchd-togail. A' cleachdadh bathar-bog 3D ùr aig a bheil comas gun shamhail, nì luchd-rannsachaidh oidhirp air fuasglaidhean fhaighinn air cùisean-iongnaidh Notre-Dame. An tèid aca air togalach a sheas troimh ochd linn chaochlaideach a chàradh?
On April 15, 2019, a huge fire consumed Notre-Dame’s roof, taking down its arrow, piercing its vaults and weakening the walls. After a year of consolidation work, 200 scientists entered the cathedral, aiming to study this world-renowned monument which holds a series of enigmas and revelations.
Archaeologists, historians and architects worked hand in hand on this unprecedented project: for months, they studied the cathedral's collapsed medieval arch. While collecting, organising and analysing every block, they discovered precious marks inscribed in the stone - until now hidden. The memory of gestures left by men more than 800 years ago. Will they be able to rebuild such medieval arches and vaults, key elements of the structure’s durability?
This film unveils the genesis of this tremendous cathedral, highlighting the mastery of its architects and builders. Thanks to new 3D software, researchers can work to solve Notre-Dame’s enigmas.

programme.title: Skipinnish Aig A' Chaisteal
programme.desc:
Skipinnish le December ann an cuideachd na mìltean de luchd-leantainn aig cuirm-chiùil a’ comharrachadh 25 bliadhna de Skipinnish, bho Chaisteal Dhùn Èideann.
Skipinnish perform December in front of thousands of fans at a concert celebrating 25 years of the band, from Edinburgh Castle. Executive Producer - Alasdair McCuish Musician - Angus MacPhail Production Manager - Gillian MacLean.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc:
Nuair a tha Bing a’ cluich geama le fòn-làimhe Flop, chaneil rudan a’ dol mar bu chòir oir tha am fòn-làimhe a' briseadh nuair a tha e dol na sgeing air an làr. An àite seo innse do Flop, tha Bing ga chuir dhan bhiona. Tha e faireachdainn cho dona mun seo ach tha e ag ionnsachadh gum feum e innse mar a thachair.
When Bing is playing a game with Flop’s mobile phone, he accidentally drops the mobile and it breaks. Instead of telling Flop, he throws it in the bin. He feels upset about it all and learns that it’s best to tell the truth. Bing - Benny Walsh Flop - Iain Mackinnon Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid Producer - May Smart Editor - Phil Reed Writer - Mairi Morrison.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc:
Nuair a tha Bing aig cuirm sa phàirc, tha còir aige 'n oidhch' a chrìochnachadh ach tha e air bhioran agus tha e fàs cho diùid. Ge-tà, le taic bho charaidean, tha e faighinn seachad air na duilgheadasan sin agus tha e a' seinn Òran a’ Bhogha-fhroise.
When Bing is at a show in the park, he is extremely nervous as he is meant to be singing the finale. However, with help from his friends, Bing gets over all his insecurities and sings the Rainbow Song. Bing - Benny Walsh Flop - Iain Mackinnon Sula - Holly Duffy Amma - Evelyn Coull MacLeod Pando - Finlay Morrison Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid Producer - May Smart Editor - Phil Reed Writer - Mairi Morrison.

programme.title: Abadas
programme.desc:
Tha Ben a' leughadh sgeulachd dha na h-Abadas mus tig iad dhan leabaidh. Aig deireadh na sgeòil, tha iad airson an geama fhaclan a chlcuich, 's tha Hari ga fhaighinn fhèin sa ghàrradh a' coimhead son cailleach-oidhche.
Before going to bed, Ben reads Seren, Hari and Ela a story. When the story ends, the Abadas decide to play the word game and this sends Hari to a windy garden looking for an owl.

programme.title: Cleasan Ataidh & Tilidh/The Adventures of Abney & Teal
programme.sub-title: A’ Lorg nam Boga-bogadach/The Poc-Poc Hunt ║ CleasanAtaidh&Tilidh/TheAdventures/Abney&TealS1E10/52
programme.desc:
‘S e latha socair a th’ ann air an eilean, latha math airson a bhith dìomhain. Tha Àtaidh, Tilidh agus Nìp a’ crochadh hamag, is tha tòrr spòrs aca a’ feuchainn ri faighinn oirre. Tha na Boga-bogadaich a’ feuchainn ri faighinn oirre cuideachd, ach tha iad air an caith suas dhan adhar is a’ dol a-mach à sealladh. Càite an deach iad? Tha Àtaidh, Tilidh agus Nìp a’ falbh a’ lorg nam Boga-bogadach.
It is a lazy day on the Island. Abney, Teal and Neep put up a hammock and have a great time trying to get into it. The Poc-Pocs join in the fun but are thrown up into the air and disappear. Where have they gone? Abney, Teal and Neep go on a Poc-Poc hunt. Teal - Linda MacLeod Abney - Tony Kearney Producer - Linda MacLeod Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid Editor - Chas Chalmers Production Company - Solus Productions.

programme.title: ’S E Iasg a Th’Annam (I’m a Fish)
programme.desc:
Ged a tha riochd caran neo-àbhaisteach air a’ Bhagan-mhara, tha e den bheachd gu bheil cuid eile ann an tha nas grainnde buileach na iad.
Although the Blobfish looks rather unusual, he says that there are other fish who are even more aesthetically displeasing than him. Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid Producer - May Smart Editor - Phil Reed Writer - Ishbel Maclean.

programme.title: Peataichean/Pets
programme.desc:
Tha Eilidh NicCarmaig a’ coinneachadh ri clann agus a’ faighinn a-mach mu mar a tha iad a’ coimhead às dèidh agus a’ cluich cuide rim peataichean aig an taigh. Anns a’ phrògram seo tha Eilidh a’ cèilidh air Emily agus na coineanaich aice, Syrius agus Seumas a tha beothail agus bòidheach. Gheibh sinn a-mach barrachd mu bhith a’ coimhead às dèidh coineanaich agus mu na rudan snog is spòrsail a bhios iad a’ dèanamh còmhla. Gheibh sinn cuideachd comhairle agus fiosrachadh bho Eilidh fhèin mu bhith a’ làimhseachadh, ag oideachadh agus a’ coimhead às dèidh peataichean.
Eilidh Cormack meets young children who are pet owners. Together they show, tell and share how they care for, play and interact with their pets at home.
In this episode, Eilidh visits Emily and her adorable rabbits, Syrius and Seumas. We find out how to look after rabbits and about all the lovely stuff Emily, Syrius and Seumas get up to together. Eilidh also shares fun and interesting facts along with advice on looking after pets at home; including how best to handle, train and feed them. Presenter - Eilidh Cormack Producer - Donna Murchison Production Manager - Mairi MacKinnon.

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc:

Hilda goes to a Sparrow Scouts meeting for the first time, and there is a badge to be earned. She and her friends tidy up in the park, but things don’t work out as you would imagine! programme.title: Seòid a' Chidsin - The Kitchen Coves
programme.desc:
Tha na seòid a’ cleachdadh mustard eadar-dhealaichte gus truinnsearan inntinneach a chruthachadh. Tha ùidh aig Ruairidh ann am mustard a tha ga dhèanamh sna Hearadh agus ag iarraidh air Ùisdean reòiteag a dhèanamh leis! Tha Ùisdean a’ toirt sùil air ais air reasabaidh traidiseanta airson slios feòla le mustard, air a ghabhail le buntàta Hasselback Ruairidh. Tha Ruairidh cuideachd ag ullachadh Cearc Supreme agus a’ cur crìoch air a’ phrògram le Carpaccio Bhiotais.
The lads use different mustards to make a variety of dishes. Ruaridh is inspired by a Harris-made mustard and asks Uisdean to make ice cream, using the mustard! Uisdean looks back at a traditional recipe for Flank with mustard, accompanied by Ruaridh’s Hasselback potatoes. Ruairidh also prepares a classic, chicken supreme, and finishes off the episode with a beetroot carpaccio.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Presenter - Uisdean Macleod Presenter - Roddy Munro Executive Producer - Ishbel Maclennan Production Manager - Mairi Macleod Producer - Kenneth Stewart.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc:
Tha Joy Dunlop a’ leantainn oirre ’s i gar toirt tro cheumannan a bharrachd ann a bhith ag ionnsachadh na Gàidhlig. Bidh i a’ dèiligeadh ri facail is abairtean air measgachadh de chuspairean làitheil agus, mar thè a dh’ionnsaich na Gàidhlig i fhèin, bheir Joy mìneachadh dhuinn air briathrachas, gràmar is gnathasan-cainnte ann an dòigh a tha furasta a thuigsinn.
Coinnichidh sinn ri luchd-labhairt èasgaidh a th’ air Gàidhlig ionnsachadh gu àrd ìre neo a thogadh leis a’ Ghàidhlig air falbh bho sgìrean traidiseanta na Gàidhealtachd, agus bidh Calum MacIlleathain a’ toirt sealladh dhuinn air annasan is cuspairean ’s e air chuairt air feadh na dùthcha.
Lorgar tuilleadh stuthan taic air-loidhne aig www.speakgaelic.scot, ann am pod-chraolaidhean SpeakGaelic air BBC Sounds agus tha na prògraman air fad rin lorg le fo-thiotalan air sianal YouTube SpeakGaelic.
Joy Dunlop guides viewers through the next steps to inspire us to keep on speaking Gaelic. As in previous series, she introduces and explain usage for words and phrases on everyday topics. A Gaelic learner herself, Joy supports us through vocabulary, grammar and idiom on topics such as medicine, politics, community and exercise.
We meet diligent speakers who have embraced the language, and the intrepid Calum Maclean ventures to forgotten corners of Scotland seeking hidden treasures.
Supporting materials can be found online: www.speakgaelic.scot, in the SpeakGaelic podcasts on BBC Sounds and with English subtitles on SpeakGaelic’s YouTube channel. Presenter - Joy Dunlop Presenter - Calum Maclean Producer - Donald Macleod Executive Producer - Una MacDonald.

programme.title: Cidsin Granaidh Chalanais
programme.desc:
Gregor MacLeod inherited his grannie’s old cookery book. In it she had written down over 50 recipes by hand and Gregor has set himself the challenge of cooking his way through them.
He takes on the classics shortbread and marmalade. Grannie has five recipes for shortbread alone but Gregor has to pick one. And the instructions for marmalade are sparing, so in search of advice he visits his neighbour, a prize-winning marmalade maker.
A real challenge is grannie’s recipe for oxtail stew. He visits another neighbour, a crofter, who happens to have one in the freezer and finds out more about this cut of meat and how to cook it. And guess who is coming to tea to taste the finished stew?
For pudding, grannie’s recipe for Bakewell tart is on the menu but this time with Gregor’s 21st century twist using the marmalade he made before.
Fhuair Griogar MacLeòid seann leabhar còcaireachd a sheanmhair mar dhìleab: comhairle na làmh-sgrìobhaidh fhèin air còrr is lethcheud dinnear is greim blasta a dhèanamh. Tha Griogar a’ cur roimhe a’ dol tron a leabhar a’ feuchainn orra.
Sa phrògram seo tha e a’ cumail ri biadh as aithne dhuinn uile, aran goirid agus marmailead. Bha còig dòighean aig granaidh ar aran-goirid a dhèanamh ach feumaidh Griogar aon a thaghadh. Chan eil cus comhairle aice dha mun mharmailead, is tha sin ga chur a shireadh beachd air nàbaidh, a ghlèidh duaisean air a shon.
Fìor annas do Ghriogar, se na bh’ aice ri ràdh mu earball mairt a bhruich. Ach tha nàbaidh eile le fear reòdhta a-staigh, agus gheibh Griogar barrachd comhairle air dè nì e leis. Agus saoil cò thig ga fheuchainn nuair a bhios e bruich?Airson mìlsean, tha tort Bakewell gu bhi aige agus cuiridh e a dhreach fhèin air le marmailead na luib.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Presenter - Gregor Macleod Director - Ramsay MacMahon.

programme.title: Ath-thogail Notre-Dame/Rebuilding Notre-Dame
programme.desc:
Air a togail san dàrna linn deug ann am meadhan Paris (air an Île de la Cité), aig aon àm b' e Notre-Dame a' chathair-eaglais a b' àirde air thalamh. Tha an t-soitheach aibhseach cloiche seo a' riochdachadh ailtireachd Gotach. Ach tha a seasmhachd a-nise ann an cunnart.
Rinn an teine milleadh air cothromachd an togalaich. Chaidh am mullach a sgrios, còmhla ris a' chliath iongantaich fiodha seo – air a dèanamh de mhìle craobh daraich – 's chaidh a losgadh san teine. Ach fhathast cha do thuit Notre-Dame. Dè as coireach gu bheil i cho làidir? Am measg an sprùillich chaidh iomadh ceangal meatailt a lorg, cuid de mheud iongantach. An robh iad nam pàirt dhen chiad dhealbhadh no nach robh? An gabhadh e a bhith gun do dh'fhuiling Notre-Dame trioblaidean structarail eile tro na linntean?
Leanaidh sinn gu dlùth an luchd-saidheans is na h-ailtirean is iad a' sgrùdadh a' chliath iongantach fiodha is meatailt a bh' air cùl na cloiche. Le cuideachadh bho dhealbhan 3D agus ath-achdachaidhean gheibh sinn tuigse air toiseach an togalaich mhòrail seo.
Built in the 12th century in the centre of Paris (on Île de la Cité), Notre-Dame was once the world's highest cathedral. This gigantic stone structure is the very essence of Gothic architecture. But today, its stability is compromised.
The 2019 fire greatly damaged the building's structure. Its roof was completely destroyed, as well as its incredible wooden frame, made of a thousand oaks, which was swallowed by the flames. Still, Notre-Dame did not collapse. What are the secrets of this exceptional strength? Amongst the wreckage, many metal fasteners were found, some of incredible size. Were they part of the original design or not? Is it possible that Notre-Dame encountered other structural problems throughout the centuries?
We closely follow scientists and architects as they study the impressive skeleton of wood and metal which hid behind the stone. Supported by 3D animations as well as re-enactments, their interventions allow us to grasp the genesis of this monumental structure.
Dubbed in Gaelic with English subtitles. Narrator - Anna Murray Producer - Seumas Mactaggart Executive Producer - Shona Henderson Executive Producer - Calum McConnell Editor - Innes Macleod.

programme.title: Abigail
programme.desc:
Mar annlann a tha na thrèat air leth, tha Abigail a' dèanamh Briosgaidean Seasaman Tahini. Glè, glè bhlasta, a' brùchdadh le deagh bhlas is teòclaid geal!
For a splendid accompaniment treat, Abigail makes tahini sesame cookies. Very tasty, packed with flavour and white chocolate!
In Gaelic with English subtitles Presenter - Abigail Maciver Producer - Kenneth Stewart Production Manager - Mairi Macleod Executive Producer - Rachel Ellen Mackay.

programme.title: Sailm nan Daoine
programme.desc:
Tha Rob MacNeacail air turas gus sailm Ghàidhlig a sheinn is a sgaoileadh. ’S e film tarraingeach is togarrach a tha seo mu chumhachd na coimhearsnachd, an teaghlaich is an seasmhachd a tha a dhìth gus cànan a chumail beò.
Thòisich Rob air na sailm a ghabhail ann an Carlops gus comharrachadh ceann-bliadhna bàs athar, am bàrd Aonghas MacNeacail. Ged a tha na seiseanan a’ còrdadh ri muinntir a’ bhaile, tha Rob ga cheasnachadh fhèin a bheil còir aige a bhith a’ teagasg nan salm. Cha do dh’ionnsaich e mar a stiùireas e an t-seinn ach o chionn ghoirid, agus cha deach a thogail san eaglais. Chan eil Rob aig tàmh is e a’ faireachdainn gum feum e falbh air turas gus cluinntinn mar a bhios na Gàidheil a’ seinn nan salm anns na coimhearsnachdan a tha a’ cumail an traidisein beò.
Bheir an turas e bho na h-Eileanan an Iar gu Corcaigh an Iar, a’ leantainn seann shlighean a bheireas ceòl is beachdan ùra gu bith.
Rob MacNeacail embarks on a mission to sing Gaelic psalms. An entertaining and heartwarming film about the power of community, family and the resilience needed to keep a language alive.
Rob started singing the psalms in his home village of Carlops to mark the anniversary of the death of his father, the poet Aonghas MacNeacail. Although the sessions are popular with locals, Rob starts to question his authority to teach the psalms, as he only learned how to precent relatively recently and didn’t grow up in the church.
As spring turns to summer, Rob starts to feel restless and decides to hit the road to reconnect with his Gaelic roots and hear how psalms are sung by Gaels in the communities that nurture the tradition. His journey takes him from the Western Isles to West Cork in Ireland, following well-trodden ancient paths that unravel threads of music and ideas along the way.
In Gaelic with English subtitles Director - Jack Archer Executive Producer - John Archer Editor - James Alcock Executive Producer - Calum McConnell Production Manager - Mhairi Valentine Production Company - Hopscotch Films.

programme.title: OMC
programme.desc:

Anns an treas prògram bho shreath ùr OMC! chì sinn tuilleadh sgeidsichean loma-làn charactaran èibhinn, suidheachaidhean neònach agus ‘spoofs’ gun shamhail bho n sgrìobhadairean is cleasaichean as fheàrr a th’ann. An turas sa mòmaidean ain-fhoiseil le màthair cèile, duilgheadasan cainnt ann an obair ùr, agus duais air leth ri thogail aig am bingo!
In Gaelic with English subtitles Various - Lana Pheutan Various - Hannah McKirdy Various - Darren MacLean Various - David Walker Various - Carina MacLeod Various - Iain Beggs Director - Fiann Macleod Producer - Marie McDonald.

Seo tha i ag iarraidh orra trì diofar ghlasraich a lorg fhad ’s a tha iad cuideachd a' dèanamh deiseil airson partaidh Oidhche Shamhna. Tha treallaich gu leòr sa bhothan agus feumaidh Meaban is Moo a dhol a rùrach!
Linda visits her friends Meaban and Moo at their hut to set them fun challenges. She tasks them with finding three different vegetables while they get ready for a Halloween party. Their hut is full of junk, so Meaban and Moo just need to have a good rummage! Presenter - Linda MacLeod Production Manager - Laura Deponio Producer - Sarah MacKinnon Director - Helen Scott.

programme.title: Leum Suas air an Sguaib/Room on the Broom
programme.desc:
Tha Lìosaidh NicÌosaig, a' bhana-bhuidseach, 's an cat gu dòigheil a' seòladh air sguab. Tha a' ghaoth mhòr ag èirigh 's tha Lìosaidh a' call a h-ad, an rioban a tha na falt, 's an t-slatag a tha na làimh. Ge-ta, tha triùir charaidean eile a' nochdadh a bheir taic dhi.
The witch and the cat fly through the sky on a broomstick. The wind picks up, the witch drops her hat, her bow and her wand. Fortunately, three more friends come to her aid. Can they rescue the witch from the dragon and will there be room on the broom for all?

programme.title: An Sgoil
programme.desc:
Ged a tha na saor-làithean air tòiseachadh do sgoilearan Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche, tha latha a bharrachd aig an luchd-teagaisg airson beagan trèanaidh. Tha an t-eòlaiche-inntinn Sìleas Stern os cionn sheiseanan gus sìth agus càirdeas a stèidheachadh am measg an luchd-obrach.
Although the holidays have started for the pupils of Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche, the teachers have an in-service day. Mr Mackle is keen to establish better relationships between his staff and has invited psychologist Sìleas Stern to run team building sessions that he hopes will bring peace and harmony.

programme.title: Calum: Cogadh nan Comhlan
programme.desc:
Tha Calum airson a chòmhlann aige a thoirt à Glaschu dhan Òban airson blàr mòr ciùil a tha dol aig a' Mhòd Nàiseanta Rìoghail. Ach, le tòrr fharpaisean agus gainead tìde, chan eil cùisean a' dol mar bu chòir. Leis nach eil e furasda còmhlan a làimhseachadh aig na h-amannan as fheàrr, saoil ciamar a thèid dhaibh leis na dùbhlain mhòra a th' air thoiseach orra...
Calum aims to take his band from Glasgow to Oban for a major musical battle at the Royal National Mòd. However, with numerous competitions and time constraints, things aren't going according to plan. Managing a band is never easy even in the best of times - how will they cope with the significant challenges that lie ahead? Director - Donald Ewen MacKinnon Executive Producer - Bill MacLeod.

programme.desc:

When Cameron comes across a black eagle’s egg, he wants to keep the egg for himself - he is so stubborn! How will the gang manage to return the egg to the nest and keep it safe? Sebastian - Ellen Macdonald Adele - Mischa Macpherson Cameron - Claire Frances MacNeil Gabriel - Iona Davidson Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid Producer - May Smart Producer - Mairi Macleod Writer - Alec MacDonald.

Shaun the Sheep

The farmer decides it is time to get fit and calls on Bitzer to join him. Bitzer has other ideas and comes up with a secret plan to avoid putting in the hard work. Will his scheme catch up with him in the end?
